important.name: Four of six a-w contract tests always skip, and the docstring claims coverage that does not exist
important.summary:
The file comes from the strap-skills contract_test.tmpl, but a-w has no API or models module: harness_lib.a_w_api and harness_lib.a_w_models are not in the tree (the skill ships only commands/attach_worktree.py, attach_merge.py, attach_resolve.py). So pytest.importorskip skips test_api_heredoc_launches_the_skill_api, test_api_exports_existing_names, test_models_forbid_extra_keys and test_document_round_trips_through_its_dump on every run. They are dead tests: they cannot fail, and they never will unless someone adds modules with exactly those names. The LAUNCHER literal 'scripts/skill_api.py" a_w_api' would fail anyway, because SKILL.md launches its command through hpy and commands/attach_worktree.py. The module docstring (lines 1-4) says the file covers 'its API launcher and its models', which a-w does not have, so the commit's 'add skill contract coverage' amounts to the two frontmatter checks.

Also (roast): tests/skills/test_a_w_skill_contract.py is the strap scaffold template left unedited: test_api_heredoc_launches_the_skill_api, test_api_exports_existing_names, test_models_forbid_extra_keys and test_document_round_trips_through_its_dump all start with pytest.importorskip on harness_lib.a_w_api / harness_lib.a_w_models, and neither module exists (a-w is a commands/ driver skill with no API or models). They can never run, so they can never fail; the commit 'add skill contract coverage' really adds two frontmatter checks (name and a 'Use when' prefix). No other *_skill_contract.py in tests/skills uses this skip-template, so it is not a repo convention either. Four green-looking skips are coverage theatre with extra steps.
fix: Delete MODELS, API, LAUNCHER, _module and the four API/models tests (lines 18-25, 38-60), and change the docstring to cover only the frontmatter checks that remain.

Swap the four tests for checks that fit a-w: the SKILL.md body holds the hpy launch line for ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/commands/attach_worktree.py, and every commands/*.py file that SKILL.md names exists under plugin_root()/skills/a-w/commands.

Delete the four importorskip tests together with MODELS, API, LAUNCHER and _module, and reword the module docstring to say the file checks the SKILL.md frontmatter; refreeze a-w (the r1.1 freeze pins this file's blob 8a3b87b).

Replace them with assertions on what a-w actually has: SKILL.md launches commands/attach_worktree.py through hpy, and the exit-code section's 'attach is dropped' bullet names --abort as no longer applying; refreeze a-w afterwards.

minor.name: Release note line stacks two 'before' clauses
minor.summary: docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:301-302 reads 'now resets the worktree to its HEAD before the attach before it drops the attach state'. The double 'before' is hard to parse: it can read as a reset that happens before the attach.
fix: Rephrase as 'now resets the worktree to the HEAD it had before the attach, then drops the attach state'.

minor.name: SKILL.md kept/dropped split misses the ambiguous-rule refusal, which drops the state without saying so
minor.summary:
The reworded exit-1 bullet (SKILL.md:105-112) now states that inside the loop a refusal either keeps the attach state or drops it, and keys the agent's next step on the error saying 'the attach state is kept' or 'the attach is dropped'. settle_stop (attach_resolve.py:155-158) calls restore(), which clears the state, but its refusal reads '<rules error>; the attach stopped and the worktree is back at <sha>', so it says neither. An agent that cannot match it to a bullet falls back to step 3 of the resolution loop (SKILL.md:89-90) and runs --abort, which refuses because no attach is stopped. The old text said only that 'some refusals' left the worktree rebased, so the new, stronger either/or claim is what exposes the gap.

Also (skill_package, roast): SKILL.md:104-112 now says a refusal inside the resolution loop 'either keeps the attach state or drops it' and keys the agent's next step on the error text ('the error says the attach state is kept' / 'the error says the attach is dropped'). settle_stop (attach_resolve.py:155-158) is a third drop path: rules naming both sides for a conflicted path at a rebase stop call restore(), which clears the state, and the error reads '...; the attach stopped and the worktree is back at <sha>'. That wording says neither 'kept' nor 'dropped', and the state file is gone so keep_hint adds nothing. An agent following SKILL.md has no bullet to match; 'stopped' even suggests the exit-2 stop, so a --continue rerun that refuses with 'no attach is stopped' is the likely next move. The SKILL parenthetical list of drop cases also leaves this one out.

Also (roast): The rewritten exit-1 section now says a refusal inside the loop 'either keeps the attach state or drops it', and tells the agent to classify by whether the error says 'the attach state is kept' or 'the attach is dropped'. settle_stop's ambiguous-rule refusal restores the worktree and clears the state but says 'the attach stopped and the worktree is back at <sha>', which matches neither phrase, so an agent following the two bullets has no rule for it. Rare path, but the PR is the one that made the split read as exhaustive.
fix: Reword the settle_stop refusal at plugins/harness/skills/a-w/commands/attach_resolve.py:157-158 to '...; the attach is dropped and the worktree is back at <sha>, its HEAD before the attach', so it matches the dropped bullet.
Or list the ambiguous-rule refusal in the dropped bullet at SKILL.md:109-110 (for example 'rules that name both sides for a conflicted path') and add the 'dropped' wording to the error.

Reword the settle_stop error to the shared drop phrasing, e.g. f"{exc}; the attach is dropped and the worktree is back at {state.original_head[:7]}", and add 'rules that name both sides for a path at a rebase stop' to the drop list in SKILL.md:109-110 (both files are frozen in docs/plans/freezes/skill/a-w/r1.1-freeze.json, so the edit needs a refreeze).
Reword settle_stop's message to '...; the attach is dropped and the worktree is back at <sha>' so it lands in the second bullet.
Or add 'a rule conflict at a rebase stop' to the parenthetical list in SKILL.md's 'attach is dropped' bullet and accept 'stopped' as a synonym there.

minor.name: Failed-restore branch of check_moves_something has no test
minor.summary:
check_moves_something now has two outcomes when nothing moves: restore succeeds (dropped message, covered by the two updated tests) or restore raises AttachError (state kept, message names --abort and the failed reset). The second branch, whose contract is that the state file survives so --abort can finish, is not exercised by any test in tests/skills; a regression that clears the state before the reset, or drops the --abort hint that keep_hint relies on, would pass the suite.

Also (docs): The bug this PR fixes is mostly hit by a --committed attach with no conflict: every worktree commit is already patch-equivalent in the target, so the rebase drops them all (attach_worktree.py:210-212 goes straight to land_resolved). The docstring (attach_resolve.py:267) and refusal (attach_resolve.py:278) still say 'the resolution kept the branch's copy of every path', which misdescribes that case. SKILL.md:109-110, the release note (v1.0.0.md:300-301) and SkillSpec SC-2 all describe it correctly as 'a --committed rebase that leaves nothing to move'.

Also (skill_package): When restore() fails in check_moves_something (attach_resolve.py:279-283) the error says the reset to the original HEAD failed and the state is kept, but not where the worktree now is. The parallel failure branch in unstarted (attach_resolve.py:192-196) names it ('the worktree is left at <head[:7]>'), and SKILL.md:107-108 tells the agent the worktree 'may sit at a rebased commit' in this case. The two messages for the same failure shape read differently; the head sha is already in scope as the `head` parameter.

Also (roast): check_moves_something uses one message for both modes: 'the resolution kept the branch's copy of every path, so nothing moves'. In the case this PR targets and the new test drives (a --committed attach whose commits the target already holds), git rebase drops the patch-equivalent commits with no conflict and no resolution at all, so the refusal describes something nobody did. The release note (docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:135-136) and SKILL.md:109-110 describe the case correctly; only the driver text is off, and the new test asserts only 'nothing moves', so it would not notice.

Also (roast): The new except AttachError branch (reset to original_head fails, state is kept, the message names --abort) is the safety half of the fix: it is what keeps --abort reachable when restore() cannot finish. No test drives it; the sibling branch in unstarted() (attach_resolve.py:190-196) is untested too, so a regression that clears the state before a failed reset would pass CI.

Also (tests): The fix adds a second outcome to check_moves_something (attach_resolve.py:279-283): when restore() raises, the attach state is kept and the message tells the agent to run --abort. The new and tightened tests (test_a_resolution_that_keeps_the_branch_copy_clears_the_state, test_committed_whose_commits_the_target_already_holds_restores_the_worktree) cover only the path where the reset succeeds. A regression that clears the state before the reset, or that drops the --abort hint, would pass the suite.
fix: Add a test beside test_committed_whose_commits_the_target_already_holds_restores_the_worktree that makes the reset fail (for example a refusing hook or a locked index.lock in the worktree git dir) on a resolution that keeps the branch copy, then asserts exit 1, 'resetting the worktree to' and '--abort' in stderr, and that the state file still exists.

Branch the message on state.mode at attach_resolve.py:278: for 'committed', say 'every worktree commit is already in the target, so nothing moves'. Widen the docstring at line 267 to cover a --committed rebase that drops every commit.

Add the location to the message, matching unstarted: f"{nothing}; resetting the worktree to {state.original_head[:7]} failed ({exc}); the worktree is left at {head[:7]} and the attach state is kept: run --abort once that is fixed" (refreeze the a-w freeze afterwards).

Pick the reason by mode: for state.mode == 'committed' say 'every worktree commit is already in the target, so nothing moves'; keep the current wording for staged mode. Optionally assert the committed wording in test_committed_whose_commits_the_target_already_holds_restores_the_worktree.

Add a test that makes restore() raise during check_moves_something (for example, call check_moves_something in-process with a restore patched to raise AttachError, or a worktree whose reset fails), then assert the state file still exists and the error names --abort.

Add an in-process test that imports attach_resolve, builds a State for a repos fixture whose resolved HEAD equals target_head, monkeypatches attach_resolve.restore to raise AttachError, calls check_moves_something, and asserts the raised message holds 'so the attach state is kept' and '--abort' and that the state file written beforehand still exists.
